subject: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch', and handoff
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orchidhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch'

Marcus / team,

We are targeting the private deployment handoff this Saturday (09/18). Before we flip traffic we need a quick cross-check:

- Confirm the telemetry endpoints (DD/Prometheus) are ingesting both control-plane and inference metrics (token latency, KV cache hits, serve rate).
- Confirm we have an operational fallback (escape-hatch) that routes traffic to the hosted Redwood API if the on-prem cluster exceeds latency SLO for >2 minutes.
- Validate that the ops runbook includes a one-click flow for emergency rollback (IP reroute + WL removal).

Attached is the minimal runbook Orchid's SRE expects to see. Can you confirm readiness and call out any gaps by EOD Thurs so we can schedule the final rehearsal?

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Site Reliability Engineer, Orchid Health
Attachments: orchid_expectations_runbook.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orchidhealth.com>, Orchid SRE Team <sre@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch'

Thanks Daniel — good checklist. Quick readout and attachments below.

1) Telemetry:
- Control-plane and inference metrics are wired to the Orchid Datadog account via the Agent + StatsD exporter. Endpoints: https://dd.orchid.internal/api/v1/series (configured).
- We are sending: per-token latency (t_p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit ratio, batch sizes, GPU utilization, and request counts.
- Dashboards: link in Confluence (shared in related_links).

2) Escape-hatch / fallback plan:
- Implemented at the load balancer level (Layer 7). Policy: if p95 inference latency > 1200ms for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows OR 5xx rate > 2% 
  then route 100% traffic to Redwood-hosted variant.
- Failback: manual (ops) after confirming stability on same checks.
- Mechanism: Traffic steering using our control-plane runbooks + BGP ASN route withdraw (detailed in runbook).

3) Runbook (attached): redwood-orchid-runbook-v3.pdf — contains play-by-play for:
- Preflight checks (DNS, certs, NAT, allowlist)
- Smoke tests (simple prompt, long-prompt, KV priming)
- Canary progression (1%, 10%, 50%, 100%)
- Escape-hatch and rollback procedures (ip-route, LB rule toggles, DocuSign DC change not required)

Outstanding items we need from Orchid:
- Final allowlist for Orchids' egress NATs (IP ranges) to add to firewall.
- Confirmation that Orchid's NOC will standby during the 2-hour window.

I'll host a 30-minute run-through Thur 09/16 09:00 PDT. Please confirm availability.

Attachments: redwood-orchid-runbook-v3.pdf

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 07:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch'

Confirmed on telemetry plumbing. Notes:
- Datadog events arriving, but two tags missing on inference streams: cluster_id and deployment_tag. I pushed a small release to the exporter to include those — will be live in 10 minutes.
- Alerting: I added a composite alert (p95 latency > 1200ms OR error_rate > 2%) and wired it to Orchid PagerDuty integration (PD key confirmed).

Also added a quick self-check script to the runbook for preflight: ./scripts/preflight-telemetry-check.sh (it returns 0/1 and a short report).

- Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Observability
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch'

Couple of clarifications from the network side:
- Orchid sent a preliminary allowlist; I attached a cleaned CSV (orchid-allowlist-ips.csv) and validated NAT ranges. Please confirm the final /24 blocks for southbound egress.
- For the escape hatch we will rely on two primitives: ALB rule change (quick) + BGP withdraw (if we need L3-level pulling). The ALB toggle is the fast-day 1 action. BGP withdraw requires Orchid NOC coordination.
- NAT timeouts: we set client ephemeral mapping to 20 minutes; if Orchid wants shorter TTL for failover safety we can lower it but will increase connection churn.

If Orchid's SRE can confirm IPs by EOD Thursday we can finalize firewall entries and the rehearsal will be green.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network & Infra Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: orchid-allowlist-ips.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid Health readiness gate: telemetry endpoints, fallback 'escape-hatch'

Ran the rehearsal canary this morning (09/16 09:00 PDT). Short summary: 
- Canary job: 500 requests over 5 minutes (mix of short and long prompts).
- Results attached: canary-results-20260915.json. Key points: p50=210ms p95=620ms p99=980ms, KV cache hit 87% after priming.
- Observed two transient 502s (third-party auth token refresh); both recovered <30s and did not breach the 2% error threshold.
- Telemetry: events were received by Datadog within ~8s; alerts did not fire.

My recommendation: proceed to the rehearsal weekend as planned. During the canary I also exercised the ALB toggle to simulate the escape-hatch; traffic re-route took ~18s to converge (expected).

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: canary-results-20260915.json
